newsitem.title: UK: UK shares steady at firmer level, awaiting Dow.
newsitem.headline: UK shares steady at firmer level, awaiting Dow.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index was hovering just below the day's best levels ahead of the Dow on Monday, buoyed by Friday's sharp run-up amid growing hopes of a prudent budget on Tuesday, traders said.
The FTSE 100 index was up 35.3 points at 4,054.0 by 1411 GMT after touching a day's best of 4,055.3.
"It is incredible coming after Friday's move," said one trader. "The momentum has just carried on."
Index heavyweights Glaxo-Wellcome and British Telecom helped lead the gainers, which led some dealers to say the rise in the FTSE was exaggerated.
But second-line stocks were also faring well. The Mid-250 was up 14.2 points at 4,425.5.
"We've entered the strongest three months of any year," said Robin Griffiths, technical analyst at HSBC James Capel.
"The last correction was a downer and the next one is likely to be sideways, but from now we will be moving higher to reach 4,500 by the election."
Griffiths said the London market had been left behind. "All we are doing is catching up with what Wall Street has done already and I think the U.S. market could start consolidating now."

The Dow was expected to face slight profit-taking on Monday after a sharp 53 point gain on Friday took the average to its eleventh closing high of the month. But analysts are far from calling an end to the latest rally in blue chips.

"After its enormous run we wouldn't be surprised to see a small correction on Wall Street but with the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday it could mean that all the activity will take place at the start of the week," said one London trader.
Treasury bonds were little changed, awaiting October home sales data at 1500 GMT. The December S&P 500 future contract was off 0.05 points by 1421 GMT.

London's leading index took market watchers by surprise on Friday when it was spurred back through the key 4,000 level in its biggest one day gain for 16-months. But traders said a challenge for new highs was unlikely ahead of tomorrow's budget.

A statement on the government's position on European monetary union by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke at 1530 GMT this afternoon could also rock the boat by rekindling political uncertainties ahead of the a general election.
Overall trading volume had reached 403 million by 1429 GMT.
Glaxo Wellcome was up 18p to 994-1/2p as ABN Amro Hoare Govett prepared to upgrade its profit forecast and rating.
Shares in British Telecommunications were up 8p to 376-1/2p amid arbitrage buying linked with proposed merger partner MCI Communications MCI.O, traders said.

Lasmo was actively traded and up 4-1/2p at 225p after a Financial Times report said Lasmo and Enterprise could be re-rated after a rumoured North Sea oil acquisition. Enterprise gained 18-1/2p to 597-1/2p.

Abbey National shares rose after a report in the Sunday Times said there was talk that the banking group was poised for another acquistion as the sector consolidates. The shares put on 8-1/2p to 672p.
Meanwhile, shares in Mercury Asset Management reached a record peak, bouyed by the recent strength in UK financial markets and amid speculation that the stock could soon be added to the FTSE 100.
Elsewhere, nursing home operator Ashbourne Plc surged to a record after the company said it was approached with a bid proposal. The shares added 22p to 161p
Shares in Christian Salvesen were 3-1/2p higher at 327-1/2p after the company said it planned to spend 150 million stg on special dividends and a demerger of its hire unit.
--Elaine Hardcastle, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
